title: Player Evaluation
description: Preserves source-supported player history, skills, role, context, risks, market and format distinctions without turning extraction into a final roster recommendation.
principles: A player take may be detailed even though it is stored in one small JSON file.
Preserve every materially discussed player dimension; do not require dimensions absent from the source.
Separate long-term talent or Dynasty value from immediate role, Redraft value and market price.
Keep team, coaching, contract and cap context source-centered; player action recommendations belong to later analysis.

dimensions.description: College, prospect, career or developmental history used by the source.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain the history and explain how the source uses it in the evaluation.
detection_questions: Does the source use college history, recruiting, prior seasons or development to support the view?

dimensions.description: Traits, athletic profile, technical strengths and limitations.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the relevant traits and the fantasy mechanism attached to them.
detection_questions: Which abilities or limitations drive the source conclusion?
Are traits distinguished from situation?

dimensions.description: Past production, usage or efficiency evidence.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain the production evidence and any warning about sample size or context.
detection_questions: Does the source cite production, touches, targets, efficiency or splits?

dimensions.description: Reasons the player can gain value or outperform.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the full positive case, not only a positive label.
detection_questions: What must go right?
Which source-supported advantages create upside?

dimensions.description: Reasons the player can underperform or lose value.
detection_questions: What argues against the player?
Which weaknesses are independent of price?

dimensions.description: Expected snaps, touches, targets, assignments or depth-chart role.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve current role, plausible role changes and the mechanism connecting opportunity to fantasy value.
detection_questions: What role does the source expect?
What event could expand or reduce it?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Keep relevant competitors and explain how they affect the player rather than listing names.
detection_questions: Who competes for work?
Does the team environment cap or support the player?

dimensions.description: Coach, coordinator, scheme or personnel-use context.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the source's coaching or scheme thesis and link the player as affected context, not as the sole owner of the take.
detection_questions: Does staff philosophy materially affect the player?
Should a separate coach or scheme take also exist?

dimensions.description: Current injury, recovery, durability or availability risk.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain medical uncertainty exactly at source confidence and avoid inventing recovery certainty.
detection_questions: Does the argument depend on health, recovery or durability?

dimensions.description: Contract, salary-cap, roster-control or transaction context.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve how contract or cap affects security, competition, trade likelihood or timing.
detection_questions: Does contract structure change the player's role or mobility?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Separate immediate season value from multi-year Dynasty value when the source does.
detection_questions: Is the source view different now, later in the season or over multiple years?

dimensions.description: Dynasty, Redraft, Bestball, PPR, return-yard or other format distinctions.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve each source-supported split and do not collapse them into one verdict.
detection_questions: Does the evaluation change by format or scoring?

dimensions.description: ADP, rookie pick range, trade cost or market sentiment.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve price sensitivity and distinguish player quality from value at cost.
detection_questions: At what price does the source buy, avoid or reconsider?
Is the player better than the market or merely good?

dimensions.description: Direct comparisons, tiers or preferred alternatives.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain the comparison and the reason for the preference.
detection_questions: Who is compared directly?
What criterion breaks the tie?

dimensions.description: Host disagreement, confidence and unresolved questions.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve differing views and uncertainty without forcing consensus.
detection_questions: Do hosts disagree?
What remains unknown or conditional?

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Could a reader reconstruct why the source likes or dislikes the player without opening the transcript?
Are background, positive case, negative case, risk, role and price preserved when discussed?
Are Dynasty, Redraft and other format distinctions kept separate?
Has a team, coach or scheme thesis been inappropriately buried only inside this player take?
Does the take stop at a verdict where the source supplied a multi-step argument?
forbidden_distortions: Do not turn a source evaluation into a Mighty Giants buy, sell, cut or trade recommendation.
Do not treat opportunity as guaranteed production.
Do not collapse talent, situation and price into one undifferentiated sentiment.
Do not omit negative evidence merely because the final source verdict is positive.
Do not invent missing college, contract, injury or role details.
extension_signals: A recurring player factor appears that is not represented by an existing dimension.
A new fantasy format repeatedly changes player conclusions.
The source uses a new kind of evidence or player-development framework.
The episode exposes a player-context relationship that should become a reusable relation type.
